text:
maya (Infra): Heads-up — we're seeing a really uneven distribution of traffic for the `svc/model-serving` clusterIP in eu-west-1. ~70% of requests are landing on two endpoints while others are barely used. Retries spiking on the client side.

alex (SRE): Ugh. Any correlation with kube-proxy or ipvs restarts?

maya (Infra): No restarts in the last 48h. kube-proxy pods are Running on all nodes. I pulled `ipvsadm -Ln` on one of the nodes and weight/hash looks fine but conntrack count is high on the hotspot nodes. snippet: 
```
# ipvsadm -Ln
TCP  10.100.55.8:80 rr
  -> 10.244.0.12:8080             Masq    1      0          0
  -> 10.244.1.34:8080             Masq    1      0          0
  -> 10.244.2.56:8080             Masq    1      0          0
  -> 10.244.3.78:8080             Masq    1      0          0
```
But `kubectl get endpoints svc/model-serving -o wide` shows endpoints across many nodes.

liu (Network): Could be asymmetric hashing + flows pinned due to long-lived connections (GRPC keepalive) + MTU/fragmentation making retries route differently. Any packet loss/latency on the east-west path?

jordan (Eng ML): Model clients use persistent gRPC connections with large payloads (KV cache + chunked responses). We did see some >200ms tails during rolling window this morning. Also saw some OOMs on a couple of GPU workers that increased reconnects.

maya (Infra): I checked node metrics: hotspot nodes show much higher `tcp_retrans` and some RX dropped. MTU on those nodes is 1500, but host NICs on the same rack side are 9000 (jumbo). I suspect an MTU mismatch on the overlay between hosts and NIC offload + RDMA configured on GPU nodes.

alex (SRE): That matches past incidents — when RDMA/efa-like drivers interact with ipvs + vxlan we get fragmentation and ipvs flow pinning to a small subset. Steps I'd try: 1) confirm overlay MTU, 2) check `ethtool -k` offloads, 3) test disabling LRO/GRO on the affected nodes, 4) rotate kube-proxy to IPVS fallback or restart kube-proxy on hotspot node to rebalance conntrack entries.

liu (Network): Also check `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward` and `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` on nodes. RDMA stacks sometimes bypass kernel path and confuse conntrack. If we can't fix quickly, we should put a node selector to drain noisy nodes from the GPU pool.

maya (Infra): I'm going to run a quick `ss -tnp` and snapshot conntrack from the hotspot node and then `kubectl cordon` + `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets` for one of the overloaded nodes to see if traffic evens out.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback triggered for revision model-serving:v2 -> v1 (reason: elevated retries on endpoint 10.244.0.12). :warning:

jordan (Eng ML): FYI the v2 rollout did increase persistent conn use, but shouldn't cause 70/30 split. Could be compounding. I'll pause new rollouts until infra confirms.

alex (SRE): If draining rebalances, we can mark this as an IPVS/east-west networking incident. If not, next: dump kube-proxy ipvs conntrack, check `ipvsadm -lcn` counters, and compare `kube-proxy --proxy-mode=ipvs` versions across nodes. Also note any kube-proxy config differences (sync-period, excludeCIDRs).

maya (Infra): Update: after draining node-17-gpu, traffic redistributed fairly across endpoints, retries went down to baseline. I still captured conntrack dump to /tmp/conntrack-dump-1710700000.log and uploaded to s3://infra-debug/1710700000/ for analysis.

liu (Network): Great. Next steps: schedule maintenance to unify MTU/offload settings across GPU nodes, and audit RDMA driver versions. I'll open a ticket and add recommended kernel flags.

jordan (Eng ML): Thanks — tagging me on the ticket. Also will add a small client-side backoff for reconnects to reduce retry storm during future rollouts.

alex (SRE): Nice quick containment. We'll keep this as P1 until MTU/driver follow-ups are done. :white_check_mark:
